tool_args.rationale: The short-window data show sink suppression and positive responses, but they do not establish whether slow adaptation reverses the response. A long-horizon probe directly tests that distinction before fitting and confirming the model.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the five-parameter sink-coupled dual-horizon model now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: All five observations have H ≤ 0.48. Over a short window, the slow adaptation term mainly constrains the ratio of amplitude to timescale, leaving its effect at H = 22.8 uncertain.
It can explain the gradient effect but cannot distinguish a persistent positive response from a late reversal.
Finer early-time sampling would better resolve the fast response but would not directly test slow adaptation at the forecast horizon.
